Why every sprite fills its own frame. One fixed camera scale would keep relative size for free, but the spread here is 31× across the medieval kit and 81× with ResourceBits in — the castle renders at 25 px per metre, an arrow at 788, a small ore nugget at 2043. At a scale that makes the castle readable, the nugget is six pixels. TRUE SCALE shows exactly that. Nothing is lost: manifest.json carries pxPerMeter for every sprite, so 1 / pxPerMeter restores true relative size wherever it is wanted.

Two facings, and the sun mirrors with them. Both yaws show the same front wall — only which half of the frame it lands on changes — so the key light is mirrored rather than rotated, and doors and windows stay lit in both. The geometry is not mirrored: asymmetric assets keep their real handedness, so the lumbermill’s saw stays on the saw’s side. Press F or the FACING button to compare.

Thumbnails here are 256 px WebP. The deliverables are the 512 px PNGs under kaykit_sprites/bottom_right/ and kaykit_sprites/bottom_left/, rendered from the base palette materials — no tiles, no nature, no team variants.
